newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond focus on IMF/World Bank meeting next week.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond focus on IMF/World Bank meeting next week.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund and World Bank 51st annual meeting in Washington from September 28 to October 3 will curtail primary market issuance next week, following an active week in which Eurobond market turnover rose, syndicate managers said on Friday.

There was little expected from borrowers in the dollar, French franc, mark and sterling sectors, from either investment grade or emerging market issuers, the syndicate managers at U.S., French, German and British houses added.
"We expect at least the first three days of next week to be very quiet," one syndicate offical at a major U.S. bank said.

"Although the dollar sector is in good shape, investors are still keen to source high-quality supply and secondary spreads are behaving themselves, we don't expect much supply in the sector," the U.S. syndicate official added.

"I know of no significant benchmark deals. Of course there are always arbitrage issuers out there who if you get to their very aggressive sub-LIBOR targets will do deals, like the GECC deal on Thursday."
"But a lot of the traditional sovereign and supranational issuers have issued for this year, and we expect volumes in the fourth quarter to be fairly light."
